To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
NVP resistance emerged in 62% of Ugandan women after NVP single dose prophylaxis and that 10% still harboured resistant virus at month 6.

1) NVP-resistant HIV variants were detected in 62% of women after NVP single dose; 2) resistant variants were detectable for up to 18 month after NVP prophylaxis, 3) 33% of women harboured NVP-resistant variants in proportions >1% for the first time 6–12 week after prophylaxis, and 4) the median proportion of NVP resistant virus was 1% in women infected with HIV-1
62% of women developed NVP-resistant HIV after single dose NVP prophylaxis; the rate decreased to 4% at 18 months after prophylaxis.

a major issue for HIV-1-infected pregnant women in sub-Saharan Africa.
the prevention of NVP resistance formation and the persistence of resistant virus over time in Ugandan women after NVP single dose prophylaxis.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NVP single-dosing should only be considered in women who are not eligible for a long-term ART.

the current WHO guidelines should be revised to recommend a longer period of additional postnatal medication with AZT and 2′, 3′-dideoxycytidine (ddC) or 3TC for at least 3–4 weeks to prevent NVP resistance formation and to avoid subsequent NNRTI treatment failure.
the use of NVP for the prevention of mother-to-child transmission should be avoided in settings where other antiretrovirs are available.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NVP should be used as a single-dose prophylaix only if the woman has no access to any other antiretrovirus.
the use of NVP as a single-dose for prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV-1 is still a valuable tool in resource-limited countries.

NVP resistance is common in women after single dose prophylaxis and that the resistance is persistent for at least 12 months after single dose prophlyaxis, which is important information for the choice of ART regimen.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the emergence of drug resistance after NVP single dose prophylaxis is common and can persist in a considerable proportion of women for up to 18 month.

the emergence of NRTI-resistant virus in the absence of NVP resistance is a frequent phenomenon after single-dose NVP prophylaxis and that the persistence of NVP-resistant variants in the viral quasispecies is common in Ugandan women.
